message: "background: conic-gradient(red,yellow,lime,cyan,blue,magenta,red)" is at risk in PDF/X exports (--format pdfx): Chromium emits repeating-*-gradient() and conic-gradient() in a form Ghostscript cannot convert, so it prints blank, unless the page also uses transparency and Ghostscript flattens the whole page to an image, which keeps the gradient but loses that page's live text. Plain PDF output is unaffected. Use linear-gradient() or radial-gradient() instead; for 0deg/90deg stripes write "linear-gradient(90deg, #b33 0 6px, #c8c5bf 6px 10px)" with "background-size: 10px 100%", and for anything else a small tiled image.
Property is high-risk for print/PDF (can force rasterization): mix-blend-mode

"mix-blend-mode: screen" on ".page:has(#c2-style) img" makes the page box a stacking context, so a .gp-behind image is trapped inside it and paints ABOVE the page's text instead of under it. Core keeps .page/.spread at "position: relative; z-index: auto" for this reason. This is an early source-only check; the build-time engine.layer.trapped audit is authoritative for the live ancestor chain.
